findings.issue: The batch summary, leaf_matches reason, and research note claim specific GxP capabilities that the cited snapshot does not contain. In snapshot 41d1aeee8c9827c7ae78a599ba6ef192911ecd6963d209763413f05b79aacf54.txt, the visible body text is limited to the hero section ('training management system', 'role and event-based training', 'training gaps'), module carousel, and footer. Full-text search finds no mention of GxP, SOP/policy/work-instruction revision-triggered retraining, role/job-title training matrix, 21 CFR Part 11 or Annex 11 e-signatures, audit trails, or per-person completion records. The research note nevertheless says the page explicitly states these items, and the batch entry uses them as evidence for the defining GxP training core.

If such a source cannot be obtained, narrow the batch summary, leaf_matches reason, and research note to what the snapshot actually proves (life-sciences role/event-based training management with training-gap visibility), remove the unverified SOP-retraining and Part 11/Annex 11 e-signature claims, and downgrade verification_status or record the evidence gap explicitly.

non_blocking_notes: input.json still records all five leaves as case_status 'not_searched' with empty application_ids and research_records, while batch.json and research.json record four commercial cases. Downstream bookkeeping should reconcile this stale progress metadata; it did not affect the source-by-source verification here.

For irt-rtsm, the Medrio snapshot body supports subject randomization, treatment allocation, stratification, kit assignment, inventory tracking, expiry management, resupply alerts/orders, and single/double-blind studies, and describes a cloud-based application. It does not detail kit returns, destruction, or close-out reconciliation, and 'automated resupply' in the batch summary is slightly stronger than the page's 'automated supply/resupply notifications' and site resupply orders.

For electronic-trial-master-file-etmf, the Montrium eTMF snapshot body and FAQ support TMF Reference Model 3.3.1 alignment, study TMF plans/document indexes, placeholder-based completeness, missing-document reporting, email intake, inspector access, and audit trails. Current-vs-superseded version retention is not detailed in the body, but the batch summary does not overclaim it; the research note already records this limitation.

For healthcare-quality-management, MEG's page substantively covers incident/near-miss reporting, investigations and root-cause work, risk registers, corrective actions tracked to completion, audit preparation, accreditation readiness, policy management, analytics, and PSO collaboration. It does not explicitly show mandatory quality-measure/indicator definitions or external measure-specification version tracking, so the entry should be read as a quality/risk/compliance type match rather than proof of the full measure-centric core; the research note honestly records this gap.

For infection-prevention-platform, the no-case outcome is appropriately documented: Prevexium is excluded as AI clinical guidance/rounds software, and the Sentri7 and Inovalon official pages returned HTTP 403 without body text. The Prevexium snapshot also mentions 'Salvium monitors' and 'outbreak surveillance', which the research note does not discuss; a future gap record should clarify why that monitoring does not satisfy the facility IPC core (continuous EHR/lab detection, IP review of suspected events, facility registry, and event-level NHSN reporting). This is not blocking because no application entry was added.
